title: Solving on a Restricted Interval
subject: mathematics

theory.introduction: A restricted interval limits the set of acceptable solutions.

content.text: Common intervals include 0 ≤ x < 2π and 0° ≤ x ≤ 360°.
Use the unit circle, reference angles, and periodicity to identify every solution inside the required interval.

formulas.name: One Full Revolution
formulas.explanation: One complete revolution can be represented using either degrees or radians.

examples.question: Solve cos(x) = 1/2 for 0 ≤ x < 2π.
examples.solution: The reference angle is π/3. Cosine is positive in Quadrants I and IV, giving x = π/3 and 5π/3.

key_ideas: The interval determines which answers are valid.
Use the unit circle to locate solutions.
misconceptions: Giving a general solution when a restricted interval was requested.
Missing a solution because only the principal angle was considered.
